items.title: Bernard Steinau Interview, 1978-08-01
items.q: [INTERVIEWER] His name was Pete Miller. You know, a perfectly nice man with a lot of record... [INTERVIEWEE] Well, there were, you know, there were people like this.

ctx.x: Oh, I can't. We'll have to restrict this. His name was Pete Miller. You know, a perfectly nice man with a lot of record, but he just didn't consider that style jazz. I imagine that Sharky was jazz to him and anything like that, you know, but, but just to him, any black bands didn't play jazz.

Well, there were, you know, there were people like this. You did have, you did have, uh, Nick LaRocca claiming that he invented jazz, as other people have claimed before and since. And, uh, I suspect if you take the right rationalization, you can come up with it. You've got a, you've got a great story, maybe this isn't the place for it, about, uh, the people up on the bayou who invented jazz. That ought to be put down sometime. I don't even remember that. That's, you know, when you and Fred Ramsey were, were up…
